vectors.description: minimal SUBSCRIBE with no parameters
SUBSCRIBE with multi-element namespace

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x01 (Relative Start) LOCATION_FILTER, StartGroup=0: the start Location is {Largest Object.Group + 1 - StartGroup, 0}, so StartGroup=0 starts at the Next Group. Open-ended. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x01, a relative StartGroup follows." Draft-20 and draft-21 had no type and inferred the shape from the parameter's byte Length; draft-22 leads with a Location Filter Type instead: "The Location Filter Type dictates which optional variable-length integer fields follow, and how they are interpreted." Its numbers are not draft-19's either, whose 0x1 was Next Group Start. With every field below 128 these bytes are identical to draft-21's, where the byte after 0x21 was a Length that happened to equal the field count, so this vector cannot tell a draft-21 decoder from a draft-22 one; with-filter-next-object, with-filter-absolute-start-zero, with-filter-absolute-start-multibyte and with-filter-noncanonical-field-count are the vectors that can

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x01 (Relative Start) LOCATION_FILTER, StartGroup=3, starting 2 groups before the current group. StartGroup=1 is the current group and StartGroup=N is N-1 groups before it. Open-ended

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x05 LOCATION_FILTER, the Next Object: {Largest Object.Group, Largest Object.Object + 1}, or {0,0} if nothing has been delivered (Section 3.1.4). Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x05, no fields follow and it specifies the Next Object." Draft-21 wrote this as a two-field filter with StartGroup and StartObject both 0 (21 02 00 00); draft-22 deleted that special case, and with-filter-absolute-start-zero is what those bytes mean now. The message Length is 2 lower than draft-21's

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x02 (Absolute Start) LOCATION_FILTER (StartGroup=10, StartObject=3): the absolute start Location {10,3}. Open-ended. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x02, StartGroup and StartObject follow."

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x03 (Absolute Start, Group End) LOCATION_FILTER: start {10,3}, EndGroupDelta 10 so the End Group is 20. EndObject is omitted, which includes all objects in group 20. The range is inclusive at both ends. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x03, StartGroup, StartObject, and EndGroupDelta follow."

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x04 (Absolute Range) LOCATION_FILTER: the fully specified inclusive range {10,3} through {20,7}. Draft-19's exclusive last-Object-plus-1 end convention is gone; object 7 of group 20 is inside this range. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x04, StartGroup, StartObject, EndGroupDelta, and EndObject follow."

non-canonical SUBSCRIBE — a type 0x02 LOCATION_FILTER whose StartGroup (10) is encoded as a 2-byte varint (800a). Section 8.1: "Variable-length integers do not need to be encoded using the minimum number of bytes; any encoding length that can represent the value is valid." The byte after 0x21 is the type, 02, where draft-21 wrote a Length of 3; draft-21's 21 03 800a 03, read as draft-22, is a type 0x03 filter missing its EndGroupDelta. Decode-only

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x00 LOCATION_FILTER. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x00, no fields follow and there is no Location Filter." The subscription is unfiltered, as if the parameter were absent. Byte-identical to draft-21's zero-Length filter, which meant the same

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x02 LOCATION_FILTER whose StartGroup and StartObject are both 0: the absolute start Location {0,0}, the beginning of the Track, and not the Next Object. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x02, StartGroup and StartObject follow." and "Otherwise, all fields are absolute." Draft-21 read these exact bytes as its Next Object special case; draft-22 deleted that case and gave the Next Object its own type, 0x05 (with-filter-next-object). A decoder or a subscription layer that still maps {0,0} to the Next Object fails here

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x02 LOCATION_FILTER, StartGroup=1000 (the minimal two-byte vi64 83e8) and StartObject=0. Three value bytes, two fields: the type says how many fields follow, not the byte count. Draft-21 wrote this filter as 21 03 83e8 00, which draft-22 reads as a type 0x03 filter with no EndGroupDelta. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x02, StartGroup and StartObject follow."

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x05 LOCATION_FILTER followed by GROUP_ORDER (0x22, descending=2). Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x05, no fields follow and it specifies the Next Object." So the byte after 05 is the next parameter's Type Delta, 1, giving 0x22. A decoder that still reads the byte after 0x21 as a Length takes 05 as five value bytes and runs past the message

SUBSCRIBE with a type 0x00 LOCATION_FILTER followed by GROUP_ORDER (0x22, descending=2). Type 0x00 carries no fields, so the next byte is GROUP_ORDER's Type Delta. Nothing else marks where the filter ends: Section 9.20: "Because unknown parameters cannot be skipped, the block is bounded by a parameter count rather than a length."

non-canonical SUBSCRIBE — a type 0x05 LOCATION_FILTER whose Location Filter Type is encoded as the 2-byte vi64 8005. The type is a vi64 like any other field, and Section 8.1: "Variable-length integers do not need to be encoded using the minimum number of bytes; any encoding length that can represent the value is valid." It decodes to the Next Object. Decode-only, because a sender always emits the minimal form

SUBSCRIBE with an empty FILL_PARAMETERS parameter (0x23). Its presence is what requests a fill fetch stream; every setting is inherited from the subscription. The value is a parameter block encoded as if for a separate message, so it begins with Number of Parameters — here 0. The parameter is therefore Length 1 carrying the single byte 00, not Length 0. Section 9.20.15 does not state whether the count is present; Section 9.20 defines a parameter block as count-bounded, and this corpus encodes that reading

SUBSCRIBE whose FILL_PARAMETERS carries a type 0x02 LOCATION_FILTER selecting the fill range {100,0} onward, evaluated with Fetch rules and independent of the subscription's own filter. The inner Type Delta chain starts from 0, so LOCATION_FILTER's delta is its absolute type 0x21

SUBSCRIBE whose FILL_PARAMETERS carries a type 0x05 LOCATION_FILTER. FILL_PARAMETERS keeps its own length prefix (3: Number of Parameters 1, Type Delta 0x21, type 05), but the LOCATION_FILTER inside it has none and is the same type-led form as at the top level. Section 9.20.15: "The LOCATION_FILTER inside FILL_PARAMETERS selects the fill range and is evaluated using the rules for a Fetch (see Section 9.20.9); it is independent of the subscription's own Location filter." An encoder that length-prefixes the inner filter writes 21 01 05 and a FILL_PARAMETERS length of 4

SUBSCRIBE whose FILL_PARAMETERS carries a type 0x00 LOCATION_FILTER with no inner length: the FILL_PARAMETERS length of 3 covers the count, the Type Delta 0x21 and the single type byte 00. Section 9.20.9: "If Location Filter Type is 0x00, no fields follow and there is no Location Filter." Section 9.20.15 has a parameter omitted from FILL_PARAMETERS take the subscription's value. Section 3.4 still says "When the subscription has no Location filter, or the LOCATION_FILTER inside FILL_PARAMETERS is zero-length, the fill range is the entire track up to Largest Object." Draft-22 has no zero-length form, and type 0x00 is the byte that form used, so this corpus reads an explicit type 0x00 as that case. The vector asserts the decode only

SUBSCRIBE with FILL_PARAMETERS (0x23) carrying SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY (0x20) and GROUP_ORDER (0x22), followed in the outer message by NEW_GROUP_REQUEST (0x32). The outer delta is 0x0F, resuming from 0x23, not 0x10 resuming from the last inner type 0x22: Section 9.20.15 calls the value a separate parameter scope, so the two chains do not interleave. The draft does not state either half explicitly

SUBSCRIBE with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) set to 0 — the SUBSCRIBE_OK should carry an empty Track Properties field. The field is still structurally present; this is a bandwidth opt-out, not a schema change
SUBSCRIBE with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) set explicitly to 1, its default
SUBSCRIBE with OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT parameter (5000ms)
SUBSCRIBE with SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT parameter (10000ms)
SUBSCRIBE with RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT parameter (3000ms)
SUBSCRIBE with FORWARD parameter (forward=1)
SUBSCRIBE with SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY parameter (32)
SUBSCRIBE with GROUP_ORDER parameter (descending=2)
SUBSCRIBE with NEW_GROUP_REQUEST parameter (group_id=50)
SUBSCRIBE with both OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT (3000ms) and SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT (8000ms); demonstrates type-delta ordering
SUBSCRIBE with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN parameter (REGISTER alias=1, type=0, value='secret-token')
SUBSCRIBE with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN parameter (USE_ALIAS alias=1)
SUBSCRIBE with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN parameter (USE_VALUE type=0, value='my-bearer-token')
SUBSCRIBE with OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT (5000ms), SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY (32), and GROUP_ORDER (ascending=1)
SUBSCRIBE with SUBGROUP_FILTER (0x25): SetID 0, one Subgroup ID range 2-4
SUBSCRIBE with OBJECTID_FILTER (0x26): SetID 0, one Object ID range 0-9
SUBSCRIBE with OBJECTID_FILTER (0x26) carrying two ranges 3-5 and 10-15; exercises delta-encoded Range pairs (wire: 03 02 05 05)
SUBSCRIBE with PRIORITY_FILTER (0x27): SetID 0, Publisher Priority range 0-127
SUBSCRIBE with SUBGROUP_FILTER (0x25) open-ended range starting at 5 with no end (final End omitted)
SUBSCRIBE with OBJECT_PROPERTY_FILTER (0x28): SetID 0, Object Property Type 0x0C, value range 1-3

SUBSCRIBE with INCLUDE_PROPERTIES (0x35) carrying the value 2. Section 9.20.21: "The allowed values are 0 (do not send Properties) or 1 (send Properties), and the default is 1. If an endpoint receives a value outside this range, it MUST close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION"

SUBSCRIBE whose FILL_PARAMETERS (0x23) contains a TRACK_PROPERTY_FILTER (0x29). Table 7 lists the eight parameter types that may appear inside FILL_PARAMETERS and 0x29 is deliberately not among them: "An endpoint that receives a parameter inside FILL_PARAMETERS that is not listed above MUST close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION." A relay forwarding a downstream FILL_PARAMETERS upstream has to strip it rather than pass it on
vectors.error_detail: TRACK_PROPERTY_FILTER (0x29) is not one of the eight parameter types Table 7 permits inside FILL_PARAMETERS

vectors.description: SUBSCRIBE with SUBGROUP_FILTER carrying SetID 1 rather than 0. Section 3.3.2: "Filter parameters with the same SetID are AND'd; distinct SetIDs are OR'd." The SetID is the first octet of every Range Filter value and it is not decoration, so a decoder that skipped it would read this filter's ranges out of the Property Type position on two of the five types. Identical to the with-subgroup-filter vector with the SetID octet changed, which is the whole of the difference on the wire.

SUBSCRIBE carrying SUBGROUP_FILTER twice: Subgroup 1-3 in set 0, Subgroup 10-12 in set 1. Section 3.3.2: "All other filter parameters MAY appear multiple times in a FETCH, SUBSCRIBE, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, or REQUEST_UPDATE". One parameter carries one SetID, so two alternatives that each constrain the same field have no other encoding. Section 9.20 requires that "Parameters MUST be serialized in ascending order by Type", which makes the second instance a Type Delta of 0 — the byte after the first value. A decoder that reads a zero delta as a malformed repeat rather than as a second instance closes the session on this frame.

SUBSCRIBE carrying SUBGROUP_FILTER and PRIORITY_FILTER under the same SetID, which Section 3.3.2 combines with AND: an Object passes only if its Subgroup ID is 1 to 3 and its Publisher Priority is 0 to 127. The pair beside the with-two-subgroup-filters vector is what separates the two operators — same SetID is AND, different SetIDs are OR — and neither vector alone shows which one a SetID selects. Two different types, so the Type Delta is 2 rather than 0 and no repeat is involved.

SUBSCRIBE with PRIORITY_FILTER covering 0 to 255, the whole of the field. Section 9.20.12: "If a decoded value exceeds 255, the endpoint MUST reject this with REQUEST_ERROR with error code INVALID_FILTER since Publisher Priority is an 8-bit field." 255 is the largest value that is not a rejection, and its End delta is the first in this file that does not fit a single-byte varint — 255 is written 80ff, so a decoder that read one byte per delta would resolve the range as 0-0 and then find a trailing octet it had no field for.

SUBSCRIBE with a Message Parameter type draft-22 does not define — must close the session. Section 9.20: "An endpoint that receives an unknown Message Parameter MUST close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. Because the receiver has to understand every Message Parameter, there is no need for a mechanism to skip unknown parameters. Because unknown parameters cannot be skipped, the block is bounded by a parameter count rather than a length."
vectors.error_detail: message parameter type 0x41 is not defined by draft-22

vectors.description: SUBSCRIBE whose LOCATION_FILTER carries Location Filter Type 0x06, the first value draft-22 does not define. Section 9.20.9: "Any other Location Filter Type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION." Draft-21 read the same byte as a Length of 6, so a draft-21 decoder reports an overrun here rather than an unknown type
vectors.error_detail: Location Filter Type 0x06 is not defined; draft-22 defines 0x00 through 0x05

vectors.description: truncated SUBSCRIBE — missing track_name
vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading track_name

vectors.description: SUBSCRIBE carrying AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN twice, with different Token Values. Section 8.9 is the carve-out: "An Authorization Token MAY be repeated within a message as long as the combination of Token Type and Token Value are unique after resolving any aliases." The second instance is written as a Type Delta of 0, which is the only encoding a second instance has once Section 9.20 requires ascending order. Identical to the with-auth-token-use-value vector with the count raised and a second token appended, so the only new bytes are the repeat itself.
